extracted.intended_audience: public_relations practitioners and communicators (PR writers, media-relations professionals)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluation criteria for writing press releases aimed at journalists and stakeholders, emphasizing journalistic voice, news judgment, structure, AP style, quotes, headlines, multimedia, proofreading, and strategic alignment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reads like news (not marketing copy)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt a journalistic voice rather than promotional language—focus on facts and newsworthiness so journalists see the piece as editorially useful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Has clear news value (passes journalist news judgment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Has clear news value (passes journalist news judgment)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrates why the item matters now and to whom; aligns with what journalists consider newsworthy (timeliness, impact, prominence, proximity, conflict, human interest).

rubrics_metrics.name: Inverted pyramid structure
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organize the release so the most important information appears first, with supporting detail and background following—facilitates quick editing and cut-to-fit by newsrooms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strong, specific headline
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Craft a concise, specific headline that communicates the news hook and works for both journalists and other audiences; avoid vague or purely promotional headlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: 5Ws in lead
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the lead answers who, what, when, where, and why (and how, when relevant) so readers immediately understand the core news.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quotes that journalists will actually use
rubrics_metrics.description: Quotes that journalists will actually use
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide quotable statements that add perspective or insight (not sales copy); include attribution and avoid generic platitudes so editors can lift them into stories.

rubrics_metrics.name: AP style throughout
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow AP Style conventions consistently (dates, numbers, titles, punctuation) to meet newsroom expectations and reduce editing work.

rubrics_metrics.name: No grammar/punctuation errors
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proofread carefully to eliminate mistakes that undermine credibility; use proofreading techniques and checklists to catch common grammar and punctuation issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinctive angle (not generic)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present a clear, differentiated news angle so the release stands out among routine announcements—avoid generic framing that blends in with other releases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Brand voice consistent
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain a consistent brand voice and style that aligns with organizational identity while still reading like news where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Story-driven
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure content to tell a coherent story with a clear beginning (lead), development (key facts/quotes), and context/background—help journalists see the narrative arc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multimedia included
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide supporting multimedia (images, video, infographics, links) to increase pickup and social sharing; ensure assets are high-quality and captioned appropriately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editor-ready (minimal editing required)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Format and write the release to be easily used by editors (clean structure, AP style, clear lead, usable quotes and boilerplate) so it requires minimal newsroom editing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Management-approved (legal/exec sign-off if needed)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure appropriate internal approvals and stakeholder sign-off (legal, executive, or other internal reviewers) are obtained before distribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategic alignment with org goals
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Align the release with broader organizational strategy and communications objectives so it supports measured business or reputational outcomes.
